question: Which of the following ‘V’ blocks will have one ‘V’ groove and two grooves (slots) on either side for clamping in two positions?
solution:
The correct answer is __Single level double groove ‘V’ block****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Single level double groove ‘V’ block__ is a specialized tool used in machining and inspection applications.
 
• It features one ‘V’ groove and two grooves (slots) on either side for clamping in two positions.
 
• This design allows for greater stability and flexibility when holding cylindrical workpieces during machining or inspection.
 
• It is commonly utilized in precision engineering and industrial setups for accurate alignment and holding of cylindrical objects.
 
• The grooves on either side facilitate secure clamping, which ensures the workpiece remains stable during operations.
 
• These blocks are known for their robust construction and high accuracy, making them ideal for various industrial applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Matched pair ‘V’ blocks:**
 
 
• Matched pair ‘V’ blocks are used in pairs for holding longer cylindrical workpieces to ensure uniformity.
 
• These blocks are precision-matched to provide equal height and alignment for the workpiece.
 
 
 
• **Double level single groove ‘V’ block:**
 
 
• These blocks feature a double-level design, allowing them to hold workpieces at different heights for specific machining requirements.
 
• They include one ‘V’ groove and are suited for complex machining setups.
 
 
 
• **Single level single groove ‘V’ block:**
 
 
• This type of block features a single level and one ‘V’ groove, primarily designed for simpler machining tasks.
 
• It is commonly used in applications where additional grooves or slots are not required.
